chunks: That ʿAli عليه السلام ruled regarding the beard: if it was shaved and did not grow back, then the full diyyah is due; but if it grew back, then one-third of the diyyah is due.

key_terms.ثُلُثُ الدِّيَةِ: one-third of the blood money compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for shaving a man's beard if it does or does not grow back?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on compensation for injury involving the beard. Imam ʿAli عليه السلام ruled that if the beard is removed and never regrows, the full diyyah is payable, while partial compensation of one-third applies if it grows back.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5332 - In the narration of Al-Sakuni, it is reported that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled that if a man's beard was shaved off and it did not grow back, the full blood money (diyyah) must be paid.
However, if the beard grew back, only one-third of the diyyah was required.
